page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio, delivering 64 vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It operates on a KVM hypervisor, includes a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps, and does not bundle local storage or GPUs.

In benchmark testing, the ecs.r7a.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests, including encryption and extended instructions. Memory performance is highly polarized: cached small-block read bandwidth is exceptionally strong at 4144.0 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read and write bandwidths fall into the average tier at 76.39 GB/sec and 35.1 GB/sec, respectively. The instance also shows strong capabilities in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, ray tracing, and image processing, alongside average performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving.

Given its high memory density and strong multi-threaded processing capabilities, this instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale caching layers, in-memory databases, and data analytics. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention. However, the lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which should be factored into the overall architectural cost. The instance offers a balanced qualitative cost-to-performance ratio for enterprise applications requiring substantial memory footprints without the need for hardware acceleration.
